thread:
Maya: Hey - follow-up from the RFC review earlier. Two related concerns popped up that I want quick feedback on: (1) a deferred-shedder that buffers requests for a short warmup window vs immediately shedding to lower tiers, and (2) 'kv-warmup ripples' where prewarming a shard causes transient bursty load and latency spikes for other tenants. TL;DR: want a small experiment plan and a safe default config.

Jon: ack. can you sketch the failure modes you care about? is this mostly cold-start token cost or long-tail queueing? :thinking:

Maya: Primarily long-tail queueing and transient head-of-line delays. Example: tenant A misses kvcache -> we prewarm a shard, that prewarm causes 50ms extra GPU jobs that contend with steady traffic from tenant B. If we accept all prewarm requests we hurt latency SLO; if we shed them immediately we lose quality. Deferred-shedder idea: accept prewarm requests into a short-lived buffer (100-200ms) and drain them with a low-priority window. If buffer exceeds threshold, start shedding.

Samir: Sounds sensible. For simulation, we should model: arrival distribution, p(kv-miss|tenant), shard prewarm cost, priority weights. quick pseudo:```
if kvcache.miss and warmup_credit > 0:
  accept and warmup_credit -= token_cost
else:
  if now - miss_ts < deferred_window_ms:
    enqueue(prewarm_queue, req)
  else:
    route_to-fallback_or_reject()
```
We can tune warmup_credit by tenant SLA/cost class.

Leo: caution: complexity explosion. deferred buffer + per-tenant warmup_credit + spill queues = lots of knobs. How do we avoid cross-tenant resource leakage? e.g., tenant X exhausting warmup_credit for shard Y affecting tenant Z's warmup.

Anya: +1 to Leo. Also need observability hooks: metric for "prewarm_inflight", "prewarm_drain_latency", "shed_count_by_tenant", and alert thresholds. We should be able to flip back to immediate-shedder if we see SLO regressions.

Maya: Good point re leakage. My thought: warmup_credit is per-tenant-per-shard limited, and global prewarm_inflight cap per-GPU. That prevents one tenant from hogging. The deferred buffer should be bounded and age-out fast.

Jon: Another corner: prewarm ripples interact with autoscaler. If prewarm spikes trigger scale-up, we might oscillate. We should simulate with a simple autoscaler model (scale-latency curve + cooldown).

InfraBot: perf-sim run queued: https://perf.redwood.internal/sim/632987 - expected completion in 2h :robot_face:

Samir: I'll wire a tiny discrete-event sim this afternoon. Proposed knobs: deferred_window_ms, prewarm_queue_size, per-tenant-warmup_tokens, global_prewarm_cap, autoscale_cooldown_ms. I'll post results in the sim link.

Leo: For rollout, keep default conservative: deferred_window_ms=100ms, prewarm_queue_size=8, per-tenant-warmup_tokens=200. Feature-flag it and route 1% of traffic first. If perf is stable, ramp to 10%.

Anya: Add dashboards + synthetic probe that exercises a cold shard while measuring tail latency for unrelated tenants. That will catch ripples early. Also add an eval prompt set to detect quality loss from shedding.

Maya: Agreed. Experiment plan (short):
1) Samir runs sim and shares perf curves (QPS, p99 for unrelated tenants, prewarm throughput).
2) Add server-side metric hooks and local sim deploy behind FF for 1% traffic.
3) Run synthetic probes and compare baseline vs experiment.
4) If clean, ramp and capture cost delta.

Samir: volunteering for step 1. Will push sim + plotted curves. plan to try deferred_window_ms in [50,100,200] and prewarm_queue_size in [4,8,16].

Leo: I'll draft a short fallback policy: if p99_unrelated increases > 10% -> immediate revert to old-shedder. Also add a per-GPU prewarm hard cap to avoid autoscaler noise.

Anya: I'll add the metrics and a Grafana panel template. Also capturing shed-quality degradation metric.

Maya: Thanks all — will create the FF and small runbook. @Samir link the sim here when done and @InfraBot please post the CI checks when the server metrics PR lands. :thumbsup:

Maya: awesome. next sync in 48h unless sim shows something surprising.
